summary: Round-3 testing of BoxLogic (per-type service minutes, editable stop type, untyped-minutes modal, geocode resolution dialog). Backend: 60/60 pytest tests pass (11 new in test_types_geocode.py + 49 regression). Frontend: all 5 requested flows verified end-to-end on the public URL (config persistence, untyped modal, type dropdown recompute, geocode resolve dialog with candidate+manual, optimize with per-type service sum, colored legs + scroll regression). No blocking issues found.

issues: Clicking the backdrop closes the dialog and onClose also clears pendingImport, so all unresolved stops are silently discarded with no way to reopen the dialog (user must re-import the Excel). Suggest not closing on backdrop click, or keeping pendingImport with a 'Resolver N direcciones' button in the sidebar.
If the user selects 'Lat/Lon manual' but leaves lat/lon empty/invalid, the stop is silently skipped on confirm with no validation message.

The minutes for UNTYPED stops (untypedMin / service_time_min) can only be set through the import modal; there is no input for it in the 'Minutos por tipo de parada' row, so it cannot be changed later without re-importing.

action_items: Optional UX: don't discard pending geocode stops when the resolve dialog is dismissed (backdrop click) / allow reopening it.
Optional UX: validate empty manual lat/lon in the resolve dialog instead of silently skipping the stop.
Optional: expose the 'minutos para paradas sin tipo' value in the config panel.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~646 lines and mixes models, TSP heuristics, geocoding and routes; consider splitting into modules before it grows further.
import-excel geocodes sequentially with a 1s sleep per row; a 36-row file blocks a worker for ~36s. Consider a background job or client-side batching if files grow.
_geocode_candidates uses countrycodes=es hardcoded (same as /geocode); fine for current scope but should be config-driven if the tool is used outside Spain.
